newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN CITY BIRD CONSIDERS MORE MD PLANES.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN CITY BIRD CONSIDERS MORE MD PLANES.

text.p: City Bird, the new long-haul airline of Belgian hotel group City Hotels , said on Wednesday it was most likely to opt for McDonnell Douglas MD-11 aircraft when it decides to extend its fleet.

"For me the MD-11 is irreplacable today," City Bird and City Hotels chairman Victor Hasson told Reuters in an interview. "...but it will have to remain a high-performance plane, and evolve like all planes," he said.
City Bird, which will be launched on March 27, has already received a first MD-11 and will get a second in early June.
Hasson said he preferred the MD-11 to the Boeing 767 because it had a longer range, three engines and an important cargo capacity.
"We'll always try not to diversify the fleet too much," he added.

City Bird will offer, via leading Belgian tour operator NUR, flights from Brussels to the Dominican Republic, Cuba, Mexico and Jamaica. It will also run regular services to Miami, Orlando, Mexico and Los Angeles, San Francisco and New York.
